_comment: The town (M3). Passers-by walk in from the east along the dead-end street to a turning point and back; traffic is how many come per game hour, by the hour of day. Customers walk up to the shack door and knock: they want a product at a minimum grade and pay its stock sell price times pays, plus reputation_bonus per point of reputation (from -3 to 5) and better_tip for a better grade than asked. A request can be sold on the spot or promised for later (they come back after 2 to 4 game hours). Each game hour, every customer whose hours include it and who is not cooling down knocks with chance visit_chance, more often with reputation and when matching stock is on hand. Looks index the rows of art/people.png.

passers.name: Gus
lines: Morning! Can't stop, the watch is counting.
Is candy a carb? Don't answer that.

passers.name: Mrs. Okafor and Biscuit
lines: Biscuit thinks your shack smells like caramel.
Lovely evening for a sniff about.

passers.name: Old Mr. Haddock
lines: In my day, sugar came from the shop and we were grateful.
That pipe's not to code. Not that I'd tell anyone.

passers.name: Wendell
lines: Nothing for you today. Bills come later, they always do.
Is that a tanker? On this street?

passers.name: A man on the phone
lines: ...no, I said synergy, not sugar...
...circle back, yes, circle back...

passers.name: Skye
lines: Cool shack. Very unlicensed energy.
Do you sell anything that isn't sweet?

passers.name: Priya
lines: Something smells amazing around here.
Do you do deliveries? No? Fair.

passers.name: Bjorn
lines: Artisanal, small batch? Love that for you.
Rex, no. That's a pipe, not a tree.

passers.name: A courier
lines: Wrong street. Again.
Every app says this road goes through. It does not.

passers.name: Lou
lines: Nice night for it.
You're up late. Or early.

passers.name: A night shift nurse
lines: Twelve hours. Don't ask.
Your window's the only light on the street.

hello: Hey. Simple syrup? Head office says we buy it from them. Head office is far away.
Simple syrup again. People want vanilla everything now.
served: Perfect. Don't tell anyone where I got it.
You're a lifesaver. A sticky one.
better: This is better than the corporate stuff. Like, a lot.
order: Cool, I'll swing by after the rush.
refused: No worries. Back to the corporate goo.
waited: Guess nobody's home. Rush starts soon...
late: You promised! I've got forty lattes queued.

hello: Rich syrup, dear. For the jam. The jam has opinions.
served: Lovely. The jam will be insufferable about this.
better: Oh, this is the good stuff. The jam will win prizes. Again.
order: I'll pop back later, dear. I'm not going anywhere fast.
refused: Shop syrup it is, then. The jam will sulk.
late: You said today, dear. The jam is waiting.

hello: Hard candy, please. For the waiting room. For business reasons.
served: Excellent. Business will be booming in six months.
better: Grade A? My patients will thank me. Later, they'll thank me differently.
order: I'll come back. I'm a dentist, I'm very patient. Get it?
refused: A shame. I'll have to recommend flossing like a normal person.
waited: Nobody home. I'll leave a pamphlet. I won't, actually.
late: Promises, like teeth, should be kept.

hello: Flaky sea salt. Only flaky. I can taste the difference, and so can my lawyer.
served: Yes. Yes! This is a pyramid. Look at it.
order: Fine. Service starts at seven. Be ready.
refused: Then you are of no use to me. Good day.
waited: I do not wait. I am the one people wait for.
late: The specials board is a lie now. Because of you.

hello: Is candy a pre-workout? Asking for me.
served: Fuel! Okay, bye, my heart rate's dropping.
order: I'll do a lap and come back. A big lap.
waited: Can't stand still, losing my pace!
late: Bro. I did the lap. Twice.

hello: Sugar for the bake sale. The Lord provides, but He doesn't refine.
served: Bless you. The bake sale thanks you, the dentists more so.
better: White as a fresh choir robe. Bless.
order: I'll come back after the meeting. It's a long meeting.
refused: Ah well. We'll make do with the shop's.
waited: No answer. Patience is a virtue, but so is punctuality.
late: The scones are counting on you. And so was I.

hello: My mom said to get the good salt. I don't know what that means.
served: Is this the good salt? It looks like salt. Okay, thanks.
better: Mom's gonna be so confused. In a good way.
order: I'll come back, I guess. Mom said not to come home without it.
waited: Hello? I'm gonna be in so much trouble.
late: You said you'd have it. Mom said you'd say that.

hello: Candy for the ward. Grade A, people are suffering enough.
served: You're a saint. A sticky saint.
order: I'm on till seven. Come find me. Actually, I'll come find you.
late: I came back on my break. My only break.

hello: Good evening. Something sweet... and red. Beet syrup will do. For now.
served: Excellent. You keep such civilised hours.
better: Exquisite. One day we must talk about other... red things.
order: I shall return before dawn. Not after. Never after.
refused: A pity. I am very patient. Centuries, almost.
waited: How rude. I was not even invited in.
late: The night is short and so, it seems, is your memory.
